one_line: Young Marathi poet-philosopher of the Dnyaneshwari and early Warkari tradition under the Yadavas of Devagiri.

appearance.age_look: late teens, slim and slightly delicate build, with an understated physical presence but alert posture
appearance.face: oval face with soft jawline, medium-brown Deccan complexion, straight nose, calm large eyes with a thoughtful gaze, faint tilak in pale sandal paste on the forehead, default expression serene and introspective with a gentle half-smile
appearance.hair: straight, shoulder-length black hair parted in the middle and neatly oiled, gathered lightly at the nape into a small low knot, with a simple narrow white cotton headband tied around the forehead like a thin band of cloth
appearance.costume: simple late-13th-century Maharashtrian brahmin-style attire: an unstitched off-white cotton upper cloth (uttariya) draped over both shoulders and chest like a shawl, a long off-white cotton dhoti-style lower garment (pancha) wrapped and pleated to the ankles, both with a faint handloom texture; a pale saffron cotton angavastra folded and draped diagonally from the left shoulder to the right hip as a subtle sign of renunciation, plain wooden tulsi bead mala wrapped twice around the neck, bare forearms with no bracelets, and simple brown leather sandals on the feet; no ornate jewelry or metal ornaments, overall very modest and practical
appearance.signature: a neatly bound palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in a light brown cloth and secured with a cotton cord, cradled in his left arm, with a single slender writing stylus (reed pen) tucked into the cord

ref_desc: Dnyaneshwar is a serene late-teen Maharashtrian youth with shoulder-length black hair in a low knot, a sandal-tilak, off-white dhoti and upper cloth, pale saffron angavastra, tulsi mala, simple sandals, and a wrapped palm-leaf manuscript bundle with stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of Dnyaneshwar as a dignified late-13th-century Maharashtrian youth: a slim late-teen boy with an oval medium-brown face, calm large eyes, a faint pale sandal-tilak on his forehead, and a serene, thoughtful expression; his straight black hair is shoulder-length, parted in the middle, neatly oiled and gathered into a small low knot at the nape, with a narrow white cotton headband tied around his forehead. He wears historically grounded Deccan brahmin clothing: an off-white cotton dhoti wrapped and pleated to his ankles, and an off-white cotton upper cloth draped over both shoulders and chest like a shawl, both with subtle handloom texture, plus a pale saffron cotton angavastra folded and draped diagonally from his left shoulder to right hip as a simple renunciant’s stole. Around his neck is a plain wooden tulsi bead mala, his forearms are bare without ornaments, and he stands in simple brown leather sandals; the overall look is modest, clean and unornamented. His signature prop is a neatly bound palm-leaf manuscript bundle wrapped in light brown cloth and tied with a cotton cord, cradled gently in his left arm, with a single slender reed stylus tucked into the cord. Use a restrained palette of off-white, pale saffron, medium brown, dark brown for leather and manuscript, and soft black for hair, giving a quiet, contemplative, historically plausible presence from Yadava-era Maharashtra, shown from multiple angles to capture his consistent face, hair, garments, and manuscript bundle.
